prompt.context_jp: 先日 皆さんに助けていただいた 上野 誠の娘の実歩といいます
prompt.prompt_jp: 先日 皆さんに助けていただいた 上野 誠の娘の実歩___いいます
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits this self-introduction.

feedback.correct_en: The pattern 〜といいます is the set phrase for giving one's name. Miho is introducing herself here.
feedback.incorrect_en: を or が cannot mark the name being quoted; only と functions as the quotative marker in this self-introduction frame.

contrast_examples.en: I am his daughter, Miho (more polite).

prompt.context_jp: 実は その後の調べで 事故の原因は 上野さんの居眠りではないことが 分かりました
prompt.prompt_jp: 事故の原因___上野さんの居眠りではないことが 分かりました
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for '事故の原因' here.

feedback.correct_en: 事故の原因 is the already-established topic (everyone was blaming Ueno's dozing). The officer is now providing new info ABOUT that topic, so は marks it as the theme.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present '事故の原因' as newly introduced information, but here the cause of the accident is the known subject under discussion.

contrast_examples.jp: 事故の原因は居眠りではなかった。
contrast_examples.en: The cause (as for it) wasn't dozing off.

contrast_examples.jp: 事故の原因が判明した。

prompt.context_jp: 現場の近くに住む親子が 出頭してきたんです
prompt.prompt_jp: 現場の近くに住む親子___出頭してきたんです
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle introducing this new participant.

feedback.correct_en: The mother and son are being newly introduced to the listeners for the first time — classic new-information が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply the parent-child pair was already an established topic, but they are being revealed here as a surprise.

contrast_examples.en: A mother and son came forward (new info).

contrast_examples.jp: その親子は近所に住んでいる。
contrast_examples.en: That mother and son (already known) live nearby.

prompt.context_jp: 彼女の胸には、あの日の判断への迷い___なお、燻り続けている。
prompt.prompt_jp: あの日の判断への迷い___なお、燻り続けている
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking what is smoldering.

feedback.correct_en: 燻る is intransitive — the doubt itself is doing the smoldering, so が marks the subject of a describable state newly observed by the narrator.
feedback.incorrect_en: を would require a transitive verb (there isn't one). は would overly topicalize 'doubt' when the sentence is really describing the state of Hina's heart.

prompt.context_jp: あの場では 弦巻先生の判断が 正しいと私は思いますよ
prompt.prompt_jp: あの場では 弦巻先生の判断___正しいと私は思いますよ
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that makes this an exhaustive judgment.

feedback.correct_en: Otowa is singling out Hina's judgment specifically as the correct one (as opposed to Kitami's) — exhaustive-listing が picks her out.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would weakly topicalize her judgment and lose the pointed 'it was HERS that was right' nuance Otowa intends.

contrast_examples.jp: 弦巻先生の判断が正しい。
contrast_examples.en: It is Dr. Tsurumaki's judgment (not another's) that is right.

contrast_examples.jp: 弦巻先生の判断は正しい。
contrast_examples.en: As for Dr. Tsurumaki's judgment, it is right (generic topic).

prompt.context_jp: 喜多見チーフが 常識外れの 危険な医療行為をしたことに 変わりはありません
prompt.prompt_jp: 喜多見チーフが 危険な医療行為をしたことに 変わり___ありません
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 'no change in that fact'.

feedback.correct_en: 変わりはありません is a fixed contrastive negation pattern — 'at least this part doesn't change,' setting that fact apart from other matters.
feedback.incorrect_en: 変わりがありません sounds stilted here; the natural idiom in this concessive 'nevertheless' tone takes は to isolate what is unchanged.

prompt.context_jp: ガス処理場で爆発が起き、多数の負傷者が出ているそうだ。
prompt.prompt_jp: ガス処理場で爆発___起き、多数の負傷者が出ているそうだ
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 'an explosion' in this news report.

feedback.correct_en: News of an explosion is brand-new to the listeners — classic が for an event-reporting sentence.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply the explosion was already a known topic, but here it is just happening and being announced.

contrast_examples.jp: その爆発は大きかった。

prompt.context_jp: 音羽先生がいれば大丈夫ですよね
prompt.prompt_jp: 音羽先生___いれば大丈夫ですよね
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that picks out Otowa specifically.

feedback.correct_en: In conditional 〜ばstructures that mean 'as long as X is there,' が identifies the specific person whose presence is enough.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn Otowa into a weak topic ('as for Otowa, if he's there...'), losing the 'he in particular is sufficient' meaning Kitami intends.

contrast_examples.jp: 音羽先生がいれば大丈夫。
contrast_examples.en: If Dr. Otowa is there, it's fine (he suffices).

contrast_examples.jp: 音羽先生はいつも冷静だ。
contrast_examples.en: Dr. Otowa is always calm (topic description).

prompt.context_jp: これは 喜多見チーフの 責任感の欠如の 表れではないでしょうか
prompt.prompt_jp: これ___ 喜多見チーフの 責任感の欠如の 表れではないでしょうか
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 'this' pointing to the absence.

feedback.correct_en: これ refers to the just-mentioned fact of Kitami's absence — a known referent being characterized, which calls for topic は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present これ as new information, but it has just been pointed to in the previous sentences; the speaker is now commenting on it.

contrast_examples.jp: これは責任感の欠如だ。
contrast_examples.en: This (just mentioned) is lack of responsibility.

prompt.context_jp: 医者にできるのは ただ 目の前の命を救うことだけですよ
prompt.prompt_jp: 医者にできるのは ただ 目の前の命___救うことだけですよ
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking what the doctor saves.

feedback.correct_en: 救う is a transitive verb and 命 is its direct object — を is required.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would misread 命 as the subject, and に would mark a location/goal, not what is being saved.

prompt.context_jp: 喜多見チーフの行動によって 負傷者の命が救われたことも 事実ではないですか
prompt.prompt_jp: 喜多見チーフの行動によって 負傷者の命___救われたことも 事実ではないですか
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking 'the injured people's lives'.

feedback.correct_en: Inside the subordinate clause '〜救われたこと,' 命 is the subject of a passive event being nominalized — が marks subordinate-clause subjects naturally.
feedback.incorrect_en: は normally doesn't appear inside noun-modifying/nominalized clauses; using it here would sound unnatural and break the structure.

contrast_examples.en: The fact that lives were saved.

prompt.context_jp: 喜多見チーフの行為は 医師にあるまじきものだと 考えております
prompt.prompt_jp: 喜多見チーフの行為___ 医師にあるまじきものだと 考えております
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 'Chief Kitami's actions' in Otowa's judgment.

feedback.correct_en: Otowa is making a general evaluation about Kitami's conduct as the topic under discussion — は presents it as the theme being judged.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would spotlight the actions as newly introduced, but they have been the subject of the whole hearing; a verdict about them calls for topic は.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼の行為は許されない。
彼の行為が問題を起こした。

prompt.context_jp: 犠牲となった26名の尊い命の中に 喜多見先生のご両親がいました
prompt.prompt_jp: 犠牲となった26名の尊い命の中に 喜多見先生のご両親___いました
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 'Dr. Kitami's parents' in this revelation.

feedback.correct_en: Existence sentences with 〜に…がいる take が, especially when revealing new information — Akatsuka is disclosing a fact the audience didn't know.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make the parents a pre-established topic, undermining the dramatic revelation that they were among the victims.

contrast_examples.jp: 犠牲者の中に両親がいた。
contrast_examples.en: Among the victims were his parents (revelation).
As for his parents, they were safe (known topic).

prompt.context_jp: 彼は TOKYO MERの理念 そのものなんです
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼___ TOKYO MERの理念 そのものなんです
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 'he' in Akatsuka's closing statement.

feedback.correct_en: After a long explanation of Kitami's background, Akatsuka returns to him as the known topic and defines what he represents — classic topic は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would spotlight 'he (and no one else)', but the sentence is a thematic definition of someone the audience now knows well, not an identification question.

contrast_examples.en: He is the very embodiment of the ideal (topic definition).

prompt.context_jp: この現場 引っ張ってんのは 俺じゃない 一人の医者だ
prompt.prompt_jp: この現場 引っ張ってんの___ 俺じゃない 一人の医者だ
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 'the one leading this scene'.

feedback.correct_en: The cleft 〜のは…だ pattern uses は to set up 'the one who X' as the topic, then identifies them in the predicate.
feedback.incorrect_en: が doesn't fit the 〜のは…だ cleft frame; swapping it in breaks the structure that Komaba uses to emphasize 'the leader = a doctor.'

contrast_examples.jp: 引っ張ってるのは医者だ。
contrast_examples.en: The one leading is a doctor.

prompt.context_jp: ケガをして苦しんでる人がいます もう死んでるかもしれない
prompt.prompt_jp: ケガをして苦しんでる人___います
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 'someone suffering' in Kitami's urgent appeal.

feedback.correct_en: Kitami is asserting the existence of an injured person — 〜がいる is the standard existential pattern for presenting someone new to the discourse.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose that person is already a known topic, but Kitami is urgently pointing out they exist to justify going in.

contrast_examples.jp: その人は救助隊員です。

prompt.context_jp: なぜ 命令を無視した？
prompt.prompt_jp: なぜ 命令___無視した？
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 'orders' in Senju's angry demand.

feedback.correct_en: 無視する takes a direct object — the thing being ignored is marked with を.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make 'orders' the subject (as if the orders did the ignoring), and に doesn't fit this verb.

contrast_examples.en: To obey instructions (に with 従う).

prompt.context_jp: 「おかげさまで 順調に回復してます」
prompt.prompt_jp: ___、順調に回復してます。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the appropriate phrase for a polite reply about a recovering family member.

feedback.correct_en: おかげさまで is the set polite phrase used when reporting good news, thanking the listener for their part in it. Perfect when the MER team saved her father.
feedback.incorrect_en: ちなみに ('by the way') introduces a side note, and それにしても ('even so') expresses surprise — neither fits a grateful reply.

contrast_examples.jp: おかげさまで元気です。
contrast_examples.en: Thanks to you, I'm doing well.

contrast_examples.jp: ちなみに父は入院中です。
contrast_examples.en: By the way, my father is hospitalized.

prompt.context_jp: 私にとっては ___ 父親です
prompt.prompt_jp: 私にとっては ___ 父親です
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word Miho uses to describe her father.

feedback.correct_en: かけがえのない means 'irreplaceable' — exactly the heartfelt word for 'one and only father.'
feedback.incorrect_en: とんでもない means 'outrageous/absurd' and あっけない means 'anticlimactic'; both would insult or trivialize her father.

prompt.context_jp: ご本人に理由を ___ ところですが
prompt.prompt_jp: ここは ぜひ ご本人に理由を ___ ところですが
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the humble verb Shirogane uses for 'ask.'

feedback.correct_en: お聞きする is humble (kenjougo) — the speaker lowers herself when wanting to ask the subject. Fits a formal hearing.
feedback.incorrect_en: お聞きになる is honorific (the listener/subject does the hearing), wrong for the speaker's own action. 伺われたい mixes forms incorrectly.

contrast_examples.en: I'd like to ask the reason (humble).

prompt.context_jp: 救助活動の邪魔をされて 大変 迷惑を ___
prompt.prompt_jp: 救助活動の邪魔をされて 大変 迷惑を ___
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb that collocates with 迷惑を.

feedback.correct_en: 迷惑を被る ('to suffer inconvenience/trouble') is the fixed formal collocation Senju uses to lodge his complaint.
feedback.incorrect_en: 迷惑をもらう is not a natural collocation, and 受けさせる is a causative that reverses the direction of the harm.

contrast_examples.en: To cause trouble (fixed phrase, opposite side).

prompt.context_jp: 任命責任を ___ かねませんよ
prompt.prompt_jp: 任命責任を ___ かねませんよ
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb that fits '追及' / responsibility pressure.

feedback.correct_en: 責任を追及する is the standard political/legal collocation for 'press someone over their responsibility.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 追いかける is to physically chase, and 追い込む (to corner) doesn't collocate directly with 責任を in this frame.

contrast_examples.en: To press someone on their responsibility.

prompt.context_jp: だけど 現実は そんなに ___
prompt.prompt_jp: 現実は そんなに ___
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the adjective fitting 'reality isn't so ___.'

feedback.correct_en: 現実は甘くない is a fixed expression meaning 'reality isn't that easy/forgiving.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 辛くない ('not harsh/spicy') contradicts the point, and 優しい has the wrong polarity for Otowa's cynical remark.

prompt.context_jp: 元ハイパーレスキュー隊 隊長の血が ___ んじゃないですか？
prompt.prompt_jp: 隊長の血が ___ んじゃないですか？
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb for 'blood ___ (gets stirred up).'

feedback.correct_en: 血が騒ぐ is the idiom for 'one's blood stirs' — feeling the pull of one's former calling.
feedback.incorrect_en: 歩く and 叫ぶ don't form idioms with 血; only 騒ぐ carries this metaphorical sense.

prompt.context_jp: 「心得ております」
prompt.prompt_jp: — A: ちゃんと仕事してね。 — B: ___
prompt.prompt_en: Choose Otowa's deferential acknowledgment.

feedback.correct_en: 心得ております is a humble, formal 'I am fully aware/I know what to do' — fitting Otowa's cold obedience to Shirogane.
feedback.incorrect_en: 分かりやすい means 'easy to understand' (wrong meaning); 知っています is plain and lacks the servile register.

prompt.context_jp: The detective is correcting a prior assumption about the cause of the accident.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds more natural as the detective's revelation?

choices.text: 事故の原因は 上野さんの居眠りではないことが 分かりました。
事故の原因が 上野さんの居眠りではないことは 分かりました。

feedback.correct_en: Version A topicalizes '事故の原因' (the thing under discussion) and uses が inside the subordinate clause for the newly-discovered content — the natural flow.
feedback.incorrect_en: Version B reverses the particles: が on the main-clause topic feels abrupt, and は inside the nominalized clause breaks subordinate-clause structure.

contrast_examples.jp: 事故の原因は居眠りではないことが分かった。
contrast_examples.en: We found out that the cause wasn't dozing off.
The cause was identified (new info stand-alone).

prompt.context_jp: Kitami is telling the others he and Tokumaru will go to the site while the rest handle the hearing.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds more natural in Kitami's spoken Japanese?

choices.text: 現場には 俺と徳丸君だけで行きますんで そっちは皆さんにお任せします。
現場に 俺と徳丸君だけ行くので そっちを皆さんが任せます。

feedback.correct_en: A uses natural spoken connectives (〜ますんで) and the proper humble お任せします. The に+は contrast marks 'as for the scene' vs 'as for that side.'
feedback.incorrect_en: B's '皆さんが任せます' is backwards — 任せる means 'to entrust TO,' so '皆さんに任せる' is required. The particle choices are also unnatural.

contrast_examples.jp: 皆さんにお任せします。
contrast_examples.en: I'll leave it to all of you.

prompt.context_jp: Kitami is reassuring Nezu that he will see his daughter again.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version matches the emotional punch Kitami gives Nezu?

choices.text: 会えますよ 絶対に。
絶対に会えると思います。

feedback.correct_en: A's post-posed 絶対に adds a punchy, promise-like emphasis after the main assertion — exactly the tone of Kitami's bedside reassurance.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is grammatically fine but softer and more hedged ('I think'), which weakens the vow Kitami is making to a dying rescuer.

contrast_examples.jp: 絶対に会えると思います。
contrast_examples.en: I think you can definitely see her (hedged).

prompt.context_jp: Otowa jokes/deflects about why he came to help in the gas-filled rubble.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds more natural as Otowa's dry excuse?

choices.text: あなたを見殺しにしたら 私の査定に響いて困るんですよ。
あなたが見殺しされたら 私の査定を響かせて困るんですよ。

feedback.correct_en: 見殺しにする ('to let someone die') and 査定に響く ('to affect my evaluation') are both natural fixed collocations.
feedback.incorrect_en: B mangles both idioms: 見殺しされる isn't the natural passive, and 査定を響かせる uses the wrong valency for 響く (an intransitive verb here).

prompt.context_jp: Otowa quietly consoles Hina before the hearing.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds natural as Otowa's reassurance?

choices.text: 気にすることありませんよ。
気になることじゃありませんよ。

feedback.correct_en: 気にすることありません = 'there's nothing to worry about,' a common gentle reassurance.
feedback.incorrect_en: B swaps in 気になる (to catch one's attention) and changes the structure, producing something that doesn't convey 'don't let it bother you.'
